slides.title: Oliver Cromwell's severed head was finally buried in 1960.
Buried in Westminster Abbey
slides.body: Cromwell died in September 1658 and was laid to rest in the abbey. Then Charles II took the throne, and Parliament ordered the body dug up.

slides.title: Hanged two years after dying
slides.body: On 30 January 1661, 12 years to the day after Charles I's execution, Cromwell's corpse was hanged at Tyburn and then beheaded.

slides.title: A head on a pole
slides.body: His head was set on a pole above Westminster Hall and stayed into the 1680s. Tradition says a storm brought it down and a sentry took it home.

slides.title: Missing, then for sale
slides.body: Where it was from about 1684 to 1710 is unknown. Then it passed through collectors and showmen until the Wilkinson family bought it in 1815.

slides.title: A secret grave
slides.body: A 1934 study judged it genuine with 'moral certainty.' In 1960 it was buried at his old Cambridge college, in a spot that is still undisclosed.

caption: Dug up, hanged, beheaded, put on a pole, lost, sold, shown off, and only buried almost three centuries later. Which stage is the strangest?
xPost: Oliver Cromwell died in 1658. In 1661 his corpse was dug up, hanged and beheaded, and his head went on a pole above Westminster Hall. It passed through collectors and showmen and was only buried in 1960, in a secret spot at his old Cambridge college.
redditTitle: TIL that Oliver Cromwell's corpse was exhumed, hanged and beheaded in 1661, and that his head passed through collectors and showmen before being buried at Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, in 1960 in an undisclosed spot
